Jodie Burrage was subjected to death threats and online abuse after losing her first WTA Tour singles match in 16 months. The 27-year-old Briton, ranked 474th in the world, exited in the first round of the Chennai Open when India’s Vaishnavi Adkar recovered from a set down to win 3-6, 6-3, 7-5. As reported by BBC Sport on Tuesday, Burrage later posted an Instagram story showing a stream of direct messages that included abuse and death threats. She added the comment: “Nice welcome back to tour. I remember why I left.” German player Eva Lys publicly supported her, tagging the WTA and asking: “When will something be done?” African stars fail to match Onaolapo’s Youth Olympics feat ITF rankings: Ogunsakin breaks into world’s top 60 Dakar 2026: Nigerian duo bow out of table tennis event Burrage’s previous WTA main-draw singles appearance, outside of qualifying, was a first-round defeat at Wimbledon in July 2025. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources The incident forms part of a larger problem. Female tennis players received more than 12,000 abusive social-media posts and messages last year, according to Signify Group data, with similar numbers recorded in 2025. Angry gamblers were behind 42% of verified abuse and 59% of serious abuse cases that year. Britain’s Katie Boulter has previously spoken about receiving death threats. Players have called for identity verification on social-media platforms, while the WTA player board has described the abuse as unacceptable and potentially significant in its impact.
